model_annotation: Figure 4 is a horizontal bar chart illustrating the number of participants (N = 6) who highlighted each evaluation criterion as beneficial, with the x-axis labeled “Number of Participants” ranging from 0 to 6 in increments of 2. The y-axis lists six evaluation criteria: “Relevant FCs,” “FC Summary,” “Relevance Explanation,” “Clarity and Simplicity,” “Overall Summary,” and “Filters,” followed by “Veracity Explanation” at the bottom. Each criterion is represented by a solid green horizontal bar extending to the right, with the exact count labeled at the end of each bar. “Relevant FCs” received the highest rating with 6 participants, followed by “FC Summary” and “Relevance Explanation” both at 3, “Clarity and Simplicity” and “Overall Summary” both at 2, “Filters” at 1, and “Veracity Explanation” also at 1. The bars are arranged in descending order of participant count from top to bottom, visually emphasizing the most valued features. The chart’s title explicitly states that it reflects feedback from six participants, five journalism students and one academic, who evaluated the tool’s usability and effectiveness.
